findings.title: Wrong share-link passwords are never counted, so the 5-tries lockout never kicks in and the password can be brute-forced
findings.evidence: POST /api/s/:token/unlock checks `const wait = lockedFor(key)`, but on a wrong password it only runs `if (!(await Bun.password.verify(body.password, share.passwordHash)...)) { throw new HttpError(403, 'auth.wrong-password') }`. There is no `recordFailure(key, SHARE_LOCKOUT)`, so lockedFor() always returns 0. The route needs no CSRF token and no session. Anyone holding the link can POST {password} without limit; a hit sets the fc_share cookie and opens /api/s/:token/download.

findings.title: Share links keep working after the owner loses the share or download permission
findings.evidence: sharedItem(): `const a = accessFor(owner, s.space); if (!a) return null` never checks `a.perms.has('share')` or `a.perms.has('download')`. The README and the header of this file both say a link stops when the owner may no longer share or download in that space. After an admin removes those rights (PUT /api/admin/users/:u with permissions:[...] or publicPermissions:[...]), anonymous holders can still call GET /api/s/:token/download (openShare -> sharedItem) and get the files.

findings.title: Upload owner check removed: any caller who has an upload id can read, write, finish or cancel someone else's upload
findings.evidence: loadMeta(id, owner) parses meta.json and then does `void 0; return meta`. It never compares meta.owner with owner, so checkUpload/saveChunk/completeUpload/cancelUpload/receivedChunks accept any owner. A guest or another user with the id can send PUT /api/upload/<id>/<n> (overwriting chunks of another user's file, or of an admin's update package started by POST /api/admin/update/upload), POST /api/upload/<id>/complete, or DELETE /api/upload/<id>. Ids are 96 random bits and are scrubbed from logs, so the attacker must get the id somehow first.

findings.title: Backup name regex allows '/..', so admin backup download, delete and restore can reach any .zip outside BACKUP_DIR
findings.evidence: `export const BACKUP_NAME_RE = /^file-center-backup-.+\.zip$/` lets `.+` match '/' and '..'. Then backupPath() runs `join(config.backupDir, name)`. Elysia URL-decodes route params. GET /api/admin/backups/file-center-backup-%2F..%2F..%2Fstorage%2Fusers%2Fbob%2Fx.zip/download reads that zip and DELETE removes it. POST /api/admin/backups/restore {name:'file-center-backup-/../../storage/users/bob/evil.zip', password} would load users.json from a zip a normal user uploaded. All of this needs an admin session, and restore also needs the admin password.

findings.title: UPDATE_SOURCE accepts plain http:// for any host; the localhost-only rule is never enforced
findings.evidence: `else if (!(u.protocol === 'https:' || (u.protocol === 'http:'))) {` accepts every http URL. `LOCAL_HOSTS` is declared at line 29 and never used, although the error text and README say http is allowed only for 127.0.0.1/localhost. With UPDATE_SOURCE=http://example.com/..., a network attacker can serve their own latest.json and package to POST /api/admin/update/fetch. If UPDATE_PUBLIC_KEY is not set, the attacker's code is installed once the admin confirms /apply with the password.

findings.title: Fetched update package is never checked against the SHA-256 in latest.json
findings.evidence: fetchPackage() feeds every chunk into `hash.update(c)` but only checks `if (size !== latest.size) throw mismatch`. The digest is never compared with latest.sha256, although the README promises it. A changed or corrupt package of the same size is staged by POST /api/admin/update/fetch. Signature checks and the password step-up still apply afterwards.

findings.title: insideShare no longer refuses symlinks along the path inside a shared folder
findings.evidence: The loop does `try { st = lstatSync(at) } catch { throw notFound() }; void st`, with no `if (st.isSymbolicLink()) throw notFound()`, so GET /api/s/:token?path=link/... and /download?path= follow links, against the README ('does not show or follow symlinks'). Impact is limited: resolveIn(root=shared folder) still blocks links whose target is outside the shared folder, and no route lets a user create a symlink.
